column1: # Examples transcribed from the free public guidance of the postal authorities of Denmark, Sweden, Finland, Norway, Iceland, Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania.

# id <TAB> citation <TAB> country hint <TAB> country line (1 = the example prints it, so the test renders it) <TAB> input (a backslash-n is a line break) <TAB> expected Postal rendering <TAB> expected Display rendering (= when not pinned)

# The input is the example as printed. The Postal expectation is the printed text except where listed in docs/address-rules-tier2-c-north.md: the locality of Danish, Swedish, Finnish, Norwegian, Icelandic, Estonian and Latvian addresses is in capitals (the UPU sheets print it so; Posten Norge and the Danish address register print it in mixed case, which is the Display form),
# the Latvian and Lithuanian postcode dash is a hyphen, the Latvian locality and postcode share a line, and the trailing comma of a Latvian sub-locality is dropped.

# Sources: UPU country sheets (upu.int, addressing unit): Denmark 05/2024, Sweden 11/2024, Finland 11/2024, Norway 01/2013, Iceland 07/2002, Estonia 06/2014, Latvia 09/2023, Lithuania 06/2018; Danmarks Adresser, Gengivelse af adresse, section A.4 (danmarksadresser.dk, retrieved 2026-11-05); PostNord Sweden, Adressering; Posten Norge, Adressering (posten.no/sende/adressering, retrieved 2026-11-05).
